data.description:
## Problem

`gate_enabled` (`_commands/gates.py`) now resolves an opt-in `verify.*` review gate to a three-valued
`GateState` (ENABLED / DISABLED / UNREADABLE) — bug `steep-tired-whimbrel`. Two sibling resolvers in
`src/rebar/config.py` still collapse a config-read FAULT into the same bare bool as a deliberate
POLICY value:

* `config.mcp_readonly()` — `except ConfigError: return True`. Returns `True` both when an operator set
  `mcp.readonly` and when the config is unparseable. Consumed by `mcp_server._readonly` (write-tool
  gating) and `runner._readonly_gate` (comment-tool withholding).
* `config.mcp_gate(attr, *, fail)` — `except ConfigError: return fail`. Same collapse for
  `mcp.allow_llm` / `mcp.allow_jira_sync`, consumed by `mcp_server._mcp_gate`.

## Why this is LOWER severity than whimbrel — and still worth fixing

Both fail in the SAFE direction (readonly on, caller-chosen `fail`), so unlike `gate_enabled` neither
silently DISABLES a gate. The residual harm is diagnostic, not security: an operator whose MCP server
has gone read-only, or whose `allow_llm` tool is refused, cannot tell from the gate whether that was
their configuration or a broken config file — the same "a fault reads as a policy choice" confusion,
one layer down. There is no fail-open leak here, which is exactly why this was NOT folded into
whimbrel's small, independently-landable fix.

## Approach

Reuse `gates.GateState` rather than minting a second tri-state — that type already names these three
states and carries the `__bool__` that keeps existing bool call sites working. Note the import
direction: `config` is below `_commands` in the layering, so `GateState` likely needs to move to (or
be re-exported from) a lower module. Settle that before implementing; a second copy of the enum is the
drift this ticket exists to prevent.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `mcp_readonly()` and `mcp_gate()` distinguish an unreadable config from the configured value.
- [ ] The safe fail direction is UNCHANGED for both (no behaviour change; the information is additive).
- [ ] Exactly one tri-state type exists in the codebase; no second enum is introduced.
- [ ] The three MCP/runner consumers keep working unmodified (bool-compatibility preserved).
- [ ] A held-out test shows an unreadable config is distinguishable at each resolver, RED before GREEN.

## Provenance
Step-7 construct sweep of `steep-tired-whimbrel` (f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe). Swept every `except ConfigError`
site in `src/rebar/`; these two are the only confirmed siblings. Deliberately excluded, with reasons:
`_config_sources._pyproject_rebar_state` (already three-valued — it is the precedent whimbrel followed),
`rebar_id_audit.py:152` (explicitly fail-CLOSED and documented), `_operation_config.shadow_enabled`
(env kill-switch, not a security gate), `_engine_support/gates.py:152` (a numeric threshold default,
not an on/off gate).
data.title: MCP gate resolvers still collapse config-unreadable into the configured value
